name: actually-mcp-server
description: MCP server that matches news text to Polymarket prediction markets and returns the market's current probability - plus optional trading tools (place, sell, redeem) using your own wallet.

_comments.dependency-vulnerability-scope: 2026-09-08 audit F11. The root package.json's `overrides` only ever apply to the install root, so a consumer running `npx actually-mcp-server` used to get protobufjs@6.11.6 (via @xenova/transformers -> onnxruntime-web -> onnx-proto, critical per npm) and sharp@0.32 (high) straight from their own install tree. Fixed 2026-09-28 by bundling @xenova/transformers into dist at build time with onnxruntime-web and sharp swapped for stubs (see tsup.config.ts and src/stubs/): under Node the library only ever runs on onnxruntime-node, and this server only embeds text, so neither is used. @xenova/transformers is therefore a devDependency (the bundler's input) and onnxruntime-node 1.14.0 - the exact engine it pins - a direct dependency. Verified: embeddings from the bundled build are bit-identical to the library's own, and a consumer install contains no onnxruntime-web, onnx-proto, protobufjs 6 or sharp. An earlier attempt (reverted) bundled onnxruntime-web and onnx-proto themselves, whose CommonJS require()/__filename use does not survive esbuild's ESM output; stubbing avoids bundling that code at all. Still open for consumers: ws@8.18.0 via @ethersproject/wallet -> @ethersproject/providers (5.8.0 is the final ethers v5 release). It backs ethers' WebSocketProvider, which this package never constructs - re-evaluate if that changes. And axios@0.27.2 via @polymarket/builder-relayer-client 0.0.10 (its latest release, pinned to ^0.27.2): its advisories need an attacker-chosen URL or cookie and this package only calls fixed Polymarket hosts; moving it to axios 1.x changes the Content-Type of relayer /submit requests, which cannot be verified without a live redeem, so it waits for Polymarket's own update.
